promise: One monthly number for what your Instagram should be making, and the gap between that and what it makes now.
need: Your Instagram account with a professional (creator or business) profile
Your follower count and your reach for the last 30 days
What you earned from Instagram last month, even if it's $0
forTech: The calculator turns audience size and reach into a monthly revenue estimate. The gap between that estimate and your real income is almost always a conversion path problem, not a reach problem.
intro: You post. People like it. Your follower count goes up. Then you look at your bank account and it doesn't match.
That's the most common thing I hear from creators and coaches: I have followers but little income. It feels personal. It isn't. It's a math problem and a path problem.

I've run Meta ads for 14 years and I run my own Instagram with a DM agent every day. A following only turns into income when there's a path from the post to the sale. This calculator shows you the size of what's missing.

body: The calculator needs 2 things from you: your followers and your reach. Reach is how many different people saw your posts.

steps.title: Open your insights
steps.text: In the Instagram app, go to your profile and tap Professional dashboard. Set the dates to the last 30 days.

steps.title: Write down 3 numbers
steps.text: Your follower count, your reach for the last 30 days, and what you earned from Instagram last month. Use the real numbers, not your best month.
steps.why: If you put hopeful numbers in, you get a hopeful number out.

body: It's live and free. Open it with the button on this page.

steps.title: Enter your followers and reach
steps.text: Type in your numbers and answer anything else it asks. You'll get a monthly number back.

steps.title: Find your gap
steps.text: Take the calculator's monthly number and subtract what you earned last month. Write the result down. That's your gap.
steps.why: The number isn't a promise. It shows what a following your size can support when the path from post to sale is in place.

sections.h: Find where the gap comes from
body: A gap almost never means you need more followers. It means people who are interested have nowhere to go.
Here's the path I run: a reel, a comment keyword, a DM, a page, a checkout, then short follow-up emails. Each step hands the person to the next one. If one step is missing, people fall out there.

steps.title: Check your own path
steps.text: Paste this into Claude or ChatGPT and answer its questions.
steps.copy:
I ran an Instagram revenue calculator.

It says my Instagram should be making about: [calculator number] a month
Last month I made: [your real number]
My followers: [number]
My reach in the last 30 days: [number]

Help me find where people fall out between seeing a post and buying. Ask me one question at a time about these 6 steps: 1) what my posts tell people to do, 2) what happens when someone comments, 3) what happens in my DMs, 4) where my link sends people, 5) what I sell and for how much, 6) what follow-up I send. Then tell me the first missing step and one thing I can do about it this week. Don't guess numbers for me.

steps.title: Fix the first missing step
steps.text: Work on the first step that's missing and leave the rest for later. For most people it's what happens after someone comments.

eureka: My followers aren't the problem. The path from a comment to a sale is.
check: You have the calculator's monthly number written down
You have your gap: that number minus what you earned last month
You know the first missing step between your posts and a sale
You picked one thing to do about it this week
limits: The calculator shows the size of the gap. It doesn't close it.
The monthly number is an estimate from the numbers you enter. It isn't a promise of income.
It doesn't answer your comments or DMs for you. That's the next problem.
